name: Temu
source: Kuwayama, printed pp. 20-21 (PDF page 13): faces represented by contour and counterform.
caveat: Face recognition is a design intention, not a tested user finding. Check resemblance before adoption.

name: Lipat
idea: One ribbon turns to show its other side.
source: Logo Modernism, printed pp. 84-85 (PDF page 42): a single silhouette articulated by internal channels.
caveat: The folded band can also read as an S. It is not tied to a confirmed site name.

name: Lapisan
idea: There is more beneath the first answer.
source: Kuwayama, printed pp. 108-109 (PDF page 57): nested curves and deliberately interrupted concentric forms.
caveat: The innermost contour is the first detail to weaken at favicon size.

name: Ragam
idea: Different dimensions, without a fixed type.
source: Kuwayama, printed pp. 108-109 (PDF page 57): rotational construction; varied here by lobe length rather than repeated identical units.
caveat: The floral association is intentional. It is warmer but less specific to psychological tests.

name: Taut
idea: Two independent forms, one connected whole.
source: Kuwayama, printed pp. 108-109 (PDF page 57): interwoven bands. Open interruptions replace overprinted crossings.
caveat: Interlocking bands are a crowded trademark category. A similarity review is still required.

name: Belah
source: Logo Modernism, printed pp. 84-85 (PDF page 42): positive and negative shapes share an outer silhouette.
caveat: The organic silhouette can suggest a seed or flame. Avoid claims of treatment or transformation.

name: Raut
idea: A person revealed by the space left open.
source: Kuwayama, printed pp. 20-21 (PDF page 13): faces constructed from a containing silhouette and a profile-shaped counterform.
caveat: The facial reading is more literal than the other options. It does not imply a clinical service.

name: Pantul
source: Kuwayama, printed pp. 20-21 (PDF page 13): paired contours and faces; abstracted here into two opposing bands.
caveat: The paired curves can read as two S letters. No name is implied.

name: Mekar
source: Logo Modernism, printed pp. 84-85 (PDF page 42): directional curved bands; Kuwayama, pp. 98-99 (PDF page 52): radial construction.
caveat: The botanical association can resemble wellness brands. This is the softest direction.

name: Bidang
idea: A result has depth, not a single label.
source: Logo Modernism, printed pp. 84-85 (PDF page 42): contrasting internal planes inside a common envelope; translated here into open angular bands.
caveat: The angular band can suggest architecture or software. It is a more technical direction.

name: Jejak
idea: An individual path, not a ranking.
source: Kuwayama, printed pp. 110-113 (PDF pages 58-59): angular and returning paths; constructed here as two interdependent routes.
caveat: The route can read as a monogram. Keep its geometry separate from the eventual wordmark.

name: Inti
idea: An outer form with an unexpected interior.
source: Kuwayama, printed pp. 20-21 (PDF page 13): enclosing contours; pp. 108-109 (PDF page 57): nested shapes with an offset centre.
caveat: The narrow inner counter is the weakest detail at 16 pixels. A dedicated favicon may be needed.
